paragraphs: Friend, here is what Nahum 2 teaches me. Nineveh looked untouchable, with chariots, nobles, treasure and walls, and it still came down. Then the LORD of Hosts says, "Behold, I am against you" (Nahum 2:13). When God is the One standing against a city, no fortress, no strength and no amount of bracing can hold it.

Now look at where Nahum tucks Jacob in the middle of all that noise. Jacob's people had been laid waste, their vine ruined, and still Nahum says, "the LORD will restore the splendor of Jacob like the splendor of Israel" (Nahum 2:2). Same God, two outcomes. The proud empire gets emptied, and the ruined vine gets its splendor back. I think that's the comfort here, because the One who is against the lions is the One who keeps His promises to His own.

So here's what I'd carry out of my bakery today, baker. Nothing you pile up can stand in for being on God's side, not the biggest bank account, not the shiniest résumé, not the loudest roar. And when you feel laid waste like that vine, you aren't forgotten. I know what it is to sit in the dark with my edges worn off, and I know the LORD is the One who makes things new (Revelation 21:5).
